So the new criterion "`applied` must be `[]` and `replayedNothing` absent" is exactly "at least one step ran and it rewrote nothing". Correct, and the quickstart's `--from 17 --to 18 --json` is a non-empty range on this build. Correct.
3. `widestRange`. Non-null only when `toMajor < CHAIN_TERMINUS_MAJOR && fromMajor < CHAIN_TERMINUS_MAJOR` (meta.ts L349–352; the e2e test pins `--from T` → `{ reason: 'empty-range', widestRange: null }`). The new §3.3 paragraph describes the case `--from <target-major>` with the default `--to`, i.e. from = to = terminus — and says the JSON "says so with `replayedNothing`, whose `widestRange` names the range that would run". In that case `widestRange` is `null`: there is no wider range from that `--from`, which is the human face's "no wider range is available; check `--from`". The clause is false for the very command it explains. It does not affect the acceptance criterion (absence of the key), so S1, not M.
4. The multi-major crossing. §3.3's callout (unchanged lines) says the class of conversion `validate` cannot see exists and names the 16 → 17 crossing as holding one; the new criterion then says "the criterion that closes the gap is a replay of the last hop you ported", and the quickstart is itself a 16 → 18 flow (step 1 replays `--from 16`, acceptance replays `--from 17 --to 18`). By `composeMigrationChain`, `--from 17 --to 18` excludes step 17, so for the skill's own quickstart the acceptance replay is blind to exactly the hop the callout names as the reason the replay exists. The dev saw this (dev observation) and shipped the last-hop form, which the card body also proposed ("replay from the previous major ... as line 74 does"). The old `--from <target-major>` form was blind to every hop, so the defect is inherited, but this PR's wording is what newly scopes the promise to "the last hop" and newly pairs L74's `--from 17 --to 18` with a `--from 16` step 1 — the reader is handed a 16 → 18 recipe whose acceptance step cannot fail on a 16 → 17 chain-only residue while the paragraph above tells them that residue is why they are running it. A `--from <authored-major> --to <target-major>` range (the one step 1 replayed) is non-empty whenever the crossing has a step, catches every hop, and costs no extra words. Teaching defect in the lines this PR rewrites: M1.
5. The three extra rewordings (§3.5 row "Only the acceptance replay sees this class."; failure-mode rows "then replay the ported hop to confirm 0 changes" and "The acceptance replay still applies changes"). On the merge-base each said "the replay from the target major". After this PR §3.3 says that replay proves nothing, so a row still prescribing it would contradict the rule it points to in the same file. `git grep` over the head's `skills/objectstack-upgrade/**` finds no surviving "target major" replay wording (the only "TARGET major" left is the front-matter `compatibility:` line, which is about the installed packages, not the replay). Same file, same rule, no new content: necessary consistency, not overreach. Accepted.
6. Token ratchet. Measured: 6185 → 6147 tokens, ceiling 6188 untouched (the ratchet script is not in the diff), headroom 3 → 41; the ratchet exits 0 on both trees and its self-test passes. Paid line by line, no re-wrap: every hunk is a changed sentence or a deleted line, and the wrapped neighbours are byte-identical. Correct.
7. Cut 1: the §1 bullet "**Pending data migrations**, when the chain crosses into a major with per-deployment data gates — see below." Its content (the run prints the pending per-deployment gates when the chain crosses into such a major) survives in the §1 subsection "Data migrations are not metadata migrations" directly below, which says the run "ends by naming each one, what staying un-run costs, and that `--apply` is the only writing mode" and that every printed gate goes into the report as `pending`. The bullet carried nothing the subsection lacks. Survives.
8. Its content survives in §3.3's callout, which carries the class, the example, "necessary and not sufficient" and the replay command. What is lost is only the index entry: a reader scanning the symptom table for this symptom no longer finds a pointer to §3.3. §3.3 is on the acceptance path every reader of the skill walks (quickstart step 3 points at it), so the rule has a home. Survives; noted as the one cut with a real, small cost.
9. Evals. The file parses on both trees; evals 1 and 4 now expect `os migrate meta --from 16 --to 17 --json`, `applied: []` and `replayedNothing` absent, and say `--from 17` alone names an empty range; eval 4's `must_contain` gains `replayedNothing`, which its `expected_output` contains. Each eval's `must_contain` strings appear in its own `expected_output` (head and base). ### ④ Design judgment

Per hits file, against the card's scenario (an agent following §3.3 records a canonical-metadata acceptance that never examined anything; after PR #29045 the JSON names a run that replayed nothing):

- `skills/objectstack-upgrade/SKILL.md`, §3.3: requiring `replayedNothing` absent is the right second half — it is the CLI's own statement that a step ran, read from one function both faces share, so the skill no longer teaches a reader to infer a check happened from `applied: []`. The first half, which range to replay, is where the design falls short: "the last hop you ported" is correct for a one-major crossing and silently narrower than the crossing for every other one, while the text around it promises the replay "closes the gap" the callout describes. The card suggested the last-hop form and the dev followed it; the card also said "and/or" and asked for "a range that can fail", which `--from <authored-major> --to <target-major>` satisfies for every crossing. The quickstart L74 `--from 17 --to 18` pairs correctly with §3.3 as written, and would pair just as correctly, as `--from 16 --to 18 --json`, with the whole-range form, so the "two lines agree" requirement holds either way. The explanatory paragraph is right on `--to`'s default, on the empty range and on `todos`; wrong on `widestRange` for the command it explains (①.3). Holds except M1 and S1.
- `skills/objectstack-upgrade/SKILL.md`, §3.5 row and two failure-mode rows: the right minimal rewording; each now names the acceptance replay abstractly instead of a specific range, so they follow §3.3 wherever it lands (under M1, "the ported hop" in the `--write` row becomes "the ported range" — one word, no token cost). Holds.
- `skills/objectstack-upgrade/SKILL.md`, the two cuts: both are same-file restatements with a surviving home (①.7, ①.8). The lane's test — a cut whose content has no other home loses a rule — is met for both. Holds.
- `skills/objectstack-upgrade/evals/protocol-major-upgrade.json`: evals 1 and 4 are the two that exercise the check, the new `expected_output` says what §3.3 says and says why the old command was vacuous, and the `must_contain` addition is a string a correct answer must carry. Holds; untouched by M1 (16 → 17 crossings).

Must-fix: M1 — in §3.3 (L397–399 of the head) replace "a replay of the last hop you ported" / `os migrate meta --from <target-major − 1> --to <target-major> --json` with "a replay of the range you ported" / `os migrate meta --from <authored-major> --to <target-major> --json` (the `--from` established in §0, the same range quickstart step 1 replays), and change L74 to `os migrate meta --from 16 --to 18 --json   # \`applied\` [] and no \`replayedNothing\` (see §3.3)`; in the `--write` failure-mode row change "replay the ported hop" to "replay the ported range". Reason: `composeMigrationChain` keeps `m > fromMajor`, so the last-hop replay excludes every earlier step, and the skill's own quickstart (16 → 18) then cannot see the 16 → 17 class the callout names as the replay's purpose. Evals 1 and 4 are unchanged by this (one-hop crossings). Token cost: net zero to a few tokens; headroom is 41. Should-fix: S1 — in the same §3.3 paragraph, the clause "whose `widestRange` names the range that would run" is false for `--from <target-major>` with the default `--to` (from = to = terminus ⇒ `widestRange: null`, meta.ts L349–352, pinned by `migrate-meta-json-replayed-nothing.test.ts`); either drop the clause or say "`widestRange` is `null` there: no wider range exists from that `--from`" — the key's presence is the criterion, not its body.
